Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Certificate number: R76/2006-A-JP1-22.02
Scheme: A
Member state: Japan
Date issued: 21 December 2022 (from revision history and signature dates)
OIML issuer ID: not explicitly given

Issuing authority:
- Name: National Metrology Institute of Japan / National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (NMIJ/AIST)
- Address: AIST Tsukuba Central 3, Tsukuba Ibaraki 305-8563, Japan
- Person responsible: ISHIMURA Kazuhiko, President of AIST

Applicant:
- A&D Company, Limited
- 3-23-14 Higashi-ikebukuro, Toshima-ku, Tokyo 170-0013 JAPAN

Manufacturer:
- A&D SCALES CO., LTD.
- 191, Inseok-ro, Deoksan-myeon, Jincheon-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, 27856, KOREA

Certified type:
- Category: Non-automatic weighing instruments (module designation says "Non-automatic weighing instruments"). The schema example categories include "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... For R76 the category would be "Non-automatic weighing instrument". I'll use that.
- Type designations: All the models listed:
  SC-30KAM, SC-30KBM, SE-30KAM, SE-30KBM, SC-60KAM, SC-60KBM, SC-60KAL, SC-60KBL, SE-60KAM, SE-60KBM, SE-60KAL, SE-60KBL, SC-150KAM, SC-150KBM, SC-150KAL, SC-150KBL, SE-150KAM, SE-150KBM, SE-150KAL, SE-150KBL
- Module designation: "Non-automatic weighing instruments"
- Description: "The SC/SE series is a class III, self-indicating, non-automatic weighing instrument. The instruments are not designed for direct sales to the public."

Model family:
- family_name: "SC/SE series"
- models: 20 variants. Model-level attributes:
  - The technical data table has 3 columns by capacity group:
    - Group 1 (30K): Max = 30 kg, e = 10 g, Min = 200 g → models SC-30KAM, SC-30KBM, SE-30KAM, SE-30KBM
    - Group 2 (60K): Max = 60 kg, e = 20 g, Min = 400 g → SC-60KAM, SC-60KBM, SC-60KAL, SC-60KBL, SE-60KAM, SE-60KBM, SE-60KAL, SE-60KBL
    - Group 3 (150K): Max = 150 kg, e = 50 g, Min = 1 kg → SC-150KAM, SC-150KBM, SC-150KAL, SC-150KBL, SE-150KAM, SE-150KBM, SE-150KAL, SE-150KBL
  - Class III (all)
  - Temperature range: -10 to 40 °C (all)
  - Power supply: Dry battery (D size × 6) (all)

Model-level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity (Max): 30 kg / 60 kg / 150 kg
- verification_scale_interval (e): 10 g / 20 g / 50 g
- minimum_capacity (Min): 200 g / 400 g / 1 kg

Should I list each model individually in model_level values, or list group representatives? The schema says model_level values[]: {model, value}. I'll list all 20 models.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: III (class)
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- power_supply: "Dry battery (D size × 6)" — string value. Per rule, could record as type_level: power_supply_type or just power_supply. Battery count: D size × 6. Keep as string value.

Devices (config-ish list): initial zero-setting device ≤ 20% of Max; semi-automatic zero-setting device ≤ 4% of Max; zero-tracking ≤ 4% of Max. These could be recorded as type_level characteristics:
- initial_zero_setting_device_range: {value: {min: null, max: 20}, unit: "% of Max"} — hmm. The value is "≤ 20 % of Max". Per rule: ≤2.5m/s → {min: null, max: 2.5}. So value {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol "% of Max"? Unit symbol should be "%". Reference is Max. Maybe record:
  - initial_zero_setting_device: {value: {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol: "%", ...} with note. Simpler: record as characteristics with labels:
  - initial_zero_setting_device_max: 20% of Max? Or keep in description-level free text. The schema has components[] only for named sub-assemblies. Devices aren't components really. I could put them as type_level entries:
    - initial_zero_setting_device: {value: "≤ 20 % of Max"} — but rule says no plain strings with units... Actually rule 2 says value can be a string for formulas/symbols. For safety I'll do structured:
    - initial_zero_setting_device_range: {value: {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol: "% of Max"} — hmm, unit_symbol "% of Max" is awkward. Let me use unit_symbol "%" and add separate reference. Actually rule for 150% of Emax example: value 150, unit "%", separate safe_overload_reference "Emax". Similarly:
    - initial_zero_setting_device_limit: {value: 20, unit_symbol: "%"} with reference Max. I could add attribute "initial_zero_setting_device_limit_reference": {value: "Max"}.
    - semi_automatic_zero_setting_device_limit: {value: 4, unit_symbol: "%"}, reference Max
    - zero_tracking_limit: {value: 4, unit_symbol: "%"}, reference Max
    - semi_automatic_subtractive_tare: {value: "T = -Max"}? Tare range: -Max. Record: tare_range: {value: {min: -150?...}} hmm, T = -Max means tare equals negative Max, so min = -Max, max = 0? Actually "T = -Max" indicates subtractive tare up to Max. I'll record as string: semi_automatic_subtractive_tare: {value: "-Max"}.

Maybe simpler to keep devices as type_level characteristics with structured values where sensible.

Interfaces: RS232C serial, USB, comparator relay output. Could record as type_level: interfaces: list? Value should be single. Could record interface_serial_data: "RS232C", interface_usb: true... Maybe record as a list in description. I'll add type_level entries:
- serial_data_interface: {value: "RS232C"}
- usb_interface: {value: true}? Hmm, boolean true might be OK. Or value "USB". I'll do:
- interfaces: {value: ["RS-232C serial data interface (printer)", "USB (personal computer)", "Comparator relay output"]} — value as list of strings. The schema allows number | {min,max} | string. Lists not specified. To be safe, I'll record three separate characteristics or one string. I'll do separate:
  - serial_data_interface: {value: "RS232C"}
  - usb_interface: {value: "USB"}
  - comparator_relay_output: {value: true}? I'll use {value: "available"}... Hmm. Booleans feel cleaner: value: true. I'll use true.

Software: legally relevant software version P-1.xx (x = non-legally relevant changes). Record:
- software_version: {value: "P-1.xx"}

Sealing: tamper-evident lead and wire seal. Record:
- sealing: {value: "Tamper-evident lead and wire seal on calibration switch"}

Recommendation:
- id: R76 — canonical. The recommendation is "OIML R 76-1, Edition: 2006". id: "R76", edition: 2006, part maybe. accuracy_classes: ["III"]
- scheme: A

Test reports:
- type_evaluation_report: No. 2022-004, dated 19 Dec 2022, 5 pages. role: type_evaluation_report
- documentation file: No. 2022-004-D, dated 19 Dec 2022. role: documentation_file

Revision history:
- revision "0", date 21 December 2022 → 2022-12-21, changes "OIML Certificate first issued"

Certificate:
- number: R76/2006-A-JP1-22.02
- scheme: A
- project_number: maybe "22.02"? The number format R76/2006-A-JP1-22.02. Not clearly a project number. Omit.
- page_total: 3
- member_state: Japan
- date_issued: 2022-12-21
- oiml_issuer_id: not present; omit.

Footnotes: none.

Matrix tables: The technical data table is a matrix — 3 columns of models. I could record it as matrix_tables with name "Technical data", columns ["models", "class", "max", "e", "min", "temperature_range", "power_supply"], rows for each of the 3 model groups. That's reasonable. I'll include it.

Column units: max kg, e g, min g (or kg for 150). Let me use kg for max, g for e, g for min (1 kg = 1000 g; I'll keep "1 kg" as 1000 g? Better keep raw "1 kg"? In matrix rows I can put numeric with implied units per column units. Row: min: "1 kg" vs 1000 g. I'll put unit columns: max "kg", e "g", min "g", and value 1000 for the 150K min. Hmm, that changes representation. Alternatively keep values as strings. The matrix table rows can be objects with values; strict structured value rules apply to characteristics, matrix rows can be numeric. I'll use min: 0.2, 0.4, 1 with column unit "kg". That is clean: Min 200 g = 0.2 kg, 400 g = 0.4 kg, 1 kg. And e: 0.01, 0.02, 0.05 kg? Or keep g. Mixed units in source. I'll use column units: max kg, e g, min g → min values 200, 400, 1000. That preserves numbers.

For model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: unit kg, values for all 20 models
- verification_scale_interval: unit g, values 10/20/50
- minimum_capacity: unit g, values 200/400/1000

Model IDs: use full model designations.

Let me write model lists:
30K group: SC-30KAM, SC-30KBM, SE-30KAM, SE-30KBM
60K group: SC-60KAM, SC-60KBM, SC-60KAL, SC-60KBL, SE-60KAM, SE-60KBM, SE-60KAL, SE-60KBL
150K group: SC-150KAM, SC-150KBM, SC-150KAL, SC-150KBL, SE-150KAM, SE-150KBM, SE-150KAL, SE-150KBL

Temperature range and power supply are same across all models → type_level.

Type designations list: all 20 models.

Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" (module designation). Good.

Description: class III, self-indicating, non-automatic weighing instrument; not designed for direct sales to the public.

Devices as type_level:
- initial_zero_setting_device: {value: {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol: "% of Max"}? I'll follow the Emax pattern: unit "%", and reference noted. Actually simpler: label "initial_zero_setting_device_range" with value {min: null, max: 20}, unit_symbol "%" and I can't add reference field per strict value shape. The schema's characteristic value shape: {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. Only those keys. So I'll encode reference in unit_symbol as "% of Max"? That deviates. Alternatively encode value as string "≤ 20 % of Max". Rule 2 says formulas/symbols keep as string. "% of Max" is a relative expression; I think string value is acceptable and clear: {value: "≤ 20 % of Max", unit_symbol: null}. Hmm but "Numbers, not strings" rule... The expression is relative to Max, similar to "150% of Emax" example which they split into value 150 + unit % + separate reference characteristic. I'll do that pattern:

- initial_zero_setting_device_limit: {value: 20, unit_symbol: "%"}
- initial_zero_setting_device_limit_reference: {value: "Max"}
- semi_automatic_zero_setting_device_limit: {value: 4, unit_symbol: "%"}
- semi_automatic_zero_setting_device_limit_reference: {value: "Max"}
- zero_tracking_limit: {value: 4, unit_symbol: "%"}
- zero_tracking_limit_reference: {value: "Max"}
- semi_automatic_subtractive_tare_range: {value: "T = -Max"} — string OK.

That's verbose but conforms. Alternatively, keep devices in description only. I think including structured is better per extraction intent.

Power supply: {value: "Dry battery (D size × 6)"} — string value, unit null. Fine.

Accuracy class: type_level accuracy_class: {value: "III"}.

Software version: software_version: {value: "P-1.xx"}.

Sealing: sealing_method: {value: "Tamper-evident lead and wire seal"}.

Interfaces: 
- serial_interface: {value: "RS232C"} 
- usb_interface: {value: "USB"} — hmm redundant. Maybe:
- interfaces: {value: "RS232C serial data interface (printer), USB interface (personal computer), comparator relay output"} — single string. That's simpler and safe. I'll do individual:
  - serial_data_interface: {value: "RS232C", ...} note "to connect printer" — can't add note; fine.
  - usb_interface: {value: "USB (to connect personal computer)"}? I'll just do:
  - usb_interface: {value: "available"} no... I'll do value: true for boolean presence? JSON true is fine. Let me keep strings:
  - serial_data_interface: {value: "RS232C"}
  - usb_interface: {value: "USB"}
  - comparator_relay_output: {value: true}

Hmm, mixing. I'll just include a single "interfaces" type_level entry with a string listing. Actually the schema says type_level: <label>: {value, unit, ...}. A list value isn't in shape. String is safest.

I'll go with three separate entries as strings for machine-readability:
- serial_data_interface: {value: "RS232C"}
- usb_interface: {value: "USB"}
- comparator_relay_output: {value: true}

Recommendation: id "R76", edition 2006, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["III"]. Amendment: none. Should I include part "-1"? id canonical "R76" per rules (e.g. "R60"). Edition 2006. Good.

Test reports:
1. {id: "2022-004", date: "2022-12-19", pages: 5, role: "type_evaluation_report"}
2. {id: "2022-004-D", date: "2022-12-19", role: "documentation_file"} — pages not stated, omit.

Certificate date_issued: 21 December 2022 (signature date & revision date). Format: "2022-12-21".

Issuing authority phone/email/website: website for IAJapan accreditation is not the authority website; omit. oiml_issuer_id: omit.

Matrix table: I'll include:
{
  name: "Technical data",
  columns: ["type", "class", "max", "e", "min", "temperature_range", "power_supply"],
  column_units: [null, null, "kg", "g", "g", "°C", null],
  rows: [
    {type: "SC-30KAM, SC-30KBM, SE-30KAM, SE-30KBM", class: "III", max: 30, e: 10, min: 200, temperature_range: "-10 to 40", power_supply: "Dry battery (D size × 6)"},
    ...
  ]
}
Hmm temperature range numeric could be {min,max} but matrix row plain values. I'll keep string "-10 to 40" or object. Keep it simple: I'll omit temperature_range and power_supply from matrix rows since they're type-level, and keep matrix to per-model varying data. Actually including them with colspan is fine too. I'll include but with string values. Hmm, maybe cleaner to include only varying columns: type, max, e, min. I'll include class too since present. I'll do columns: ["models", "accuracy_class", "max", "e", "min"].

Now model_level characteristics — 20 models each for 3 attributes = 60 entries. That's fine.

Also should model_family models include attributes? Schema: models[]: model_id, label, attributes{}. I could put max/e/min in attributes per model. That duplicates model_level. The R60 example doesn't include attributes. I'll keep models minimal with model_id only, and put varying data in model_level.

Type designations: include all 20 model identifiers.

certificate.number: "R76/2006-A-JP1-22.02". project_number: omit. page_total: 3.

Let me also record issuing_authority.oiml_issuer_id — absent.

Also persons: CIML member TAKATSUJI Toshiyuki — that's signature, not person responsible of authority. person_responsible: "ISHIMURA Kazuhiko", person_title: "President of AIST".

Final JSON assembly.

For footnote_markers: none, omit.

Check decimal conversion: no commas as decimals here.

Temperature range: -10 ℃ to 40 ℃ → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C" (use canonical Unicode degree sign).

Write the JSON.
